description: The bar chart illustrates the accuracy (%) of five different reinforcement learning methods—DAPO+Self-reflection, DAPO, SRPO, PPO+Self-reflection, and PPO—across three multimodal reasoning benchmarks: Mathverse, MMLU, and Physics. The vertical axis represents accuracy percentage, ranging from 50% to 62% with tick marks at 2% intervals. The horizontal axis lists the three datasets in order: Mathverse, MMLU, and Physics. Each dataset has five grouped bars, color- and pattern-coded according to the legend: solid blue for DAPO+Self-reflection, light blue with diagonal stripes for DAPO, solid orange for SRPO, solid green for PPO+Self-reflection, and green with diagonal stripes for PPO. In Mathverse, DAPO+Self-reflection achieves ~56%, DAPO ~53%, SRPO ~55.8%, PPO+Self-reflection ~54.5%, and PPO ~53.2%. In MMLU, DAPO+Self-reflection reaches ~57%, DAPO ~56%, SRPO ~57.2%, PPO+Self-reflection ~56.2%, and PPO ~54.6%. In Physics, DAPO+Self-reflection peaks at ~61%, DAPO ~57.6%, SRPO ~60.5%, PPO+Self-reflection ~59.2%, and PPO ~57%. Across all three benchmarks, DAPO+Self-reflection consistently achieves the highest accuracy, followed closely by SRPO, suggesting that integrating self-reflection with DAPO yields the strongest performance in multimodal reasoning tasks as evaluated in this study.
